title: KCET 2022 Physics
subject: physics
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column D-1

questions.q: In case of Fraunhofer diffraction at a single slit, the diffraction pattern on the screen is described correctly by which of the following statements?
options: Central dark band having uniform brightness on either side.
Central dark band having alternate dark and bright bands of decreasing intensity on either side.
Central bright band having dark bands on either side.
Central bright band having alternate dark and bright bands of decreasing intensity on either side.
questions.explanation: In single-slit Fraunhofer diffraction the central maximum is bright and most intense; on either side there are alternately dark and bright fringes of steadily decreasing intensity.

questions.q: When a Compact Disc (CD) is illuminated by a small source of white light, coloured bands are observed. This is due to
questions.explanation: The closely spaced tracks on a CD act like a reflection diffraction grating; different wavelengths diffract at different angles, producing the coloured bands.

questions.q: Consider a glass slab which is silvered at one side and the other side is transparent. Given the refractive index of the glass slab to be 1.5. If a ray of light is incident at an angle of 45$^\circ$ on the transparent side, the deviation of the ray of light from its initial path, when it comes out of the slab is
questions.explanation: A glass slab silvered on the back behaves like a plane mirror for the incoming ray, so the net deviation is 180$^\circ$ $-$ 2i = 180$^\circ$ $-$ 2(45$^\circ$) = 90$^\circ$.

questions.q: Focal length of a convex lens will be maximum for
questions.explanation: Since $\dfrac{1}{f}=(\mu-1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}-\dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$, and red light has the smallest refractive index among the given colours, it bends the least and so gives the maximum focal length.

questions.q: For light diverging from a finite point source
options: the intensity at the wave front does not depend on the distance.
the intensity decreases in proportion to the distance squared.
questions.explanation: A point source emits spherical wavefronts; the same power spreads over a sphere of area $4\pi r^2$, so the intensity falls off as $1/r^2$, i.e. in proportion to the square of the distance.

questions.q: The fringe width for red colour as compared to that for violet colour is approximately
questions.explanation: Fringe width $\beta \propto \lambda$. Since $\lambda_{red}$ ($\approx$700 nm) is roughly double $\lambda_{violet}$ ($\approx$400 nm), the fringe width for red light is approximately double that for violet.

questions.q: In accordance with the Bohr's model, the quantum number that characterises the Earth's revolution around the Sun in an orbit of radius 1.5 $\times$ 10$^{11}$ m with orbital speed 3 $\times$ 10$^4$ m s$^{-1}$ [given mass of Earth = 6 $\times$ 10$^{24}$ kg] is
questions.explanation: Angular momentum $L=mvr=6\times10^{24}\times3\times10^4\times1.5\times10^{11}=2.7\times10^{40}$ kg m$^2$ s$^{-1}$. Using $L=n\hbar$, $n=L/\hbar \approx 2.7\times10^{40}/1.055\times10^{-34}\approx 2.57\times10^{74}$.

questions.q: An electron is revolving in its Bohr orbit having Bohr radius of 0.529 Å, then the radius of third orbit is
Binding energy of a Nitrogen nucleus $[^{14}_{7}N]$, given m$[^{14}_{7}N]$ = 14.00307 u is
In a photo electric experiment, if both the intensity and frequency of the incident light are doubled, then the saturation photo electric current
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: Saturation photocurrent depends only on the number of photons incident per second, i.e. on intensity; doubling the intensity doubles the saturation current (frequency does not affect it).

questions.q: The kinetic energy of the photoelectrons increases by 0.52 eV when the wavelength of the incident light is changed from 500 nm to another wavelength which is approximately
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: $E_{500}=1240/500=2.48$ eV. Since KE increases, the new photon energy is $2.48+0.52=3.00$ eV, giving $\lambda=1240/3.00\approx400$ nm.

questions.q: The de-Broglie wavelength of a particle of kinetic energy 'K' is $\lambda$; the wavelength of the particle, if its kinetic energy is $\dfrac{K}{4}$ is
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: $\lambda \propto 1/\sqrt{K}$; reducing K to K/4 increases $\lambda$ by a factor of $\sqrt{4}=2$, so the new wavelength is $2\lambda$.

questions.q: The radius of hydrogen atom in the ground state is 0.53 Å. After collision with an electron, it is found to have a radius of 2.12 Å, the principal quantum number 'n' of the final state of the atom is

Which logic gate is represented by the following combination of logic gates? [Figure: inputs A and B each feed a separate NOT gate (inverter); the two inverter outputs feed a NOR gate whose output is Y]
questions.explanation: Y = NOT(NOT A OR NOT B), and by De Morgan's theorem NOT(NOT A) AND NOT(NOT B) = A AND B, so the combination behaves as an AND gate.

questions.q: A metallic rod of mass per unit length 0.5 kg m$^{-1}$ is lying horizontally on a smooth inclined plane which makes an angle of 30$^\circ$ with the horizontal. A magnetic field of strength 0.25 T is acting on it in the vertical direction. When a current 'I' is flowing through it, the rod is not allowed to slide down. The magnitude of current required to keep the rod stationary is
questions.explanation: For equilibrium along the incline, the horizontal magnetic force's component balances gravity: $BI\cos\theta = \lambda g \sin\theta$, giving $I=\lambda g\tan\theta/B=(0.5\times9.8\times\tan30^\circ)/0.25\approx11.32$ A.

questions.q: A nuclear reactor delivers a power of 10$^9$ W, the amount of fuel consumed by the reactor in one hour is
questions.explanation: Energy released $E=Pt=10^9\times3600=3.6\times10^{12}$ J; mass converted $m=E/c^2=3.6\times10^{12}/9\times10^{16}=4\times10^{-5}$ kg $=0.04$ g.

questions.q: Which of the following radiations is deflected by electric field?
questions.explanation: $\gamma$-rays, X-rays and neutrons are electrically neutral, whereas $\alpha$-particles are positively charged and hence get deflected in an electric field.

questions.q: The resistivity of a semiconductor at room temperature is in between
questions.explanation: The resistivity of a semiconductor at room temperature typically lies in the broad range 10$^{-3}$ to 10$^6$ $\Omega$ cm, between that of a conductor and an insulator.

questions.q: The forbidden energy gap for 'Ge' crystal at '0'K is
questions.explanation: The band gap of germanium is close to 0.7 eV; among the given options, 0.71 eV matches this known value.

questions.q: Two masses of 5 kg and 3 kg are suspended with the help of massless inextensible strings as shown in the figure [ceiling → T$_1$ → 5 kg → T$_2$ → 3 kg, the whole system moving upward with acceleration 2 m s$^{-2}$]. When the whole system is going upwards with acceleration 2 m/s$^2$, the value of T$_1$ is (use g = 9.8 m/s$^2$)
questions.explanation: T$_1$ supports both masses accelerating upward: $T_1=(m_1+m_2)(g+a)=(5+3)(9.8+2)=8\times11.8=94.4$ N.

questions.q: The Vernier scale of a travelling microscope has 50 divisions which coincides with 49 main scale divisions. If each main scale division is 0.5 mm, then the least count of the microscope is
questions.explanation: 1 VSD $=\dfrac{49}{50}\times0.5$ mm; least count $=1$ MSD $-$ 1 VSD $=0.5\,\text{mm}\times\dfrac{1}{50}=0.01$ mm.

questions.q: The displacement 'x' (in metre) of a particle of mass 'm' (in kg) moving in one dimension under the action of a force, is related to time 't' (in sec.) by, $t=\sqrt{x}+3$. The displacement of the particle when its velocity is zero, will be
Two objects are projected at an angle $\theta$ and (90$^\circ$$-\theta$), to the horizontal with the same speed. The ratio of their maximum vertical heights is
questions.explanation: $H=\dfrac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$, so $\dfrac{H_1}{H_2}=\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^2(90^\circ-\theta)}=\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}=\tan^2\theta$.

questions.q: A car is moving in a circular horizontal track of radius 10 m with a constant speed of 10 m s$^{-1}$. A bob is suspended from the roof of the car by a light wire of length 1.0 m. The angle made by the wire with the vertical is (in radian)
questions.explanation: $\tan\theta=\dfrac{v^2}{rg}=\dfrac{100}{10\times9.8}\approx1$, so $\theta\approx\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

questions.q: A spherical oil drop carrying a net charge q is balanced in still air, with a vertical uniform electric field of strength $\dfrac{81}{7}\pi\times10^5$ V/m. When the field is switched off, the drop is observed to fall with terminal velocity 2 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ m s$^{-1}$. Here g = 9.8 m/s$^2$, viscosity of air is 1.8 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$ Ns/m$^2$ and the density of oil is 900 kg m$^{-3}$. The magnitude of 'q' is
questions.explanation: From terminal velocity, $r^2=\dfrac{9\eta v}{2\rho g}$ gives $r\approx4.29\times10^{-6}$ m, so $m=\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\rho\approx2.97\times10^{-13}$ kg. Balancing $qE=mg$: $q=mg/E\approx8\times10^{-19}$ C.

questions.q: "Heat cannot be itself flow from a body at lower temperature to a body at higher temperature". This statement corresponds to
questions.explanation: This is the Clausius statement of the second law of thermodynamics.

questions.q: A smooth chain of length 2 m is kept on a table such that its length of 60 cm hangs freely from the edge of the table. The total mass of the chain is 4 kg. The work done in pulling the entire chain on to the table is, (Take g = 10 m/s$^2$)
questions.explanation: Mass per unit length $=4/2=2$ kg/m; hanging mass $=2\times0.6=1.2$ kg with its centre of mass 0.3 m below the table. Work done $=1.2\times10\times0.3=3.6$ J.

questions.q: The angular speed of a motor wheel is increased from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. The angular acceleration of the motor wheel is
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.explanation: $\omega_1=1200\times2\pi/60=40\pi$ rad/s, $\omega_2=3120\times2\pi/60=104\pi$ rad/s; $\alpha=\dfrac{104\pi-40\pi}{16}=4\pi$ rad/s$^2$.

questions.q: The centre of mass of an extended body on the surface of the earth and its centre of gravity
options: can never be at the same point.
are always at the same point for any size of the body.
centre of mass coincides with the centre of gravity of a body if the size of the body is negligible as compared to the size (or radius) of the earth.
are always at the same point only for spherical bodies.
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.explanation: The centre of gravity coincides with the centre of mass only when the gravitational field can be treated as uniform over the body, which holds when the body's size is negligible compared to the earth's radius.

questions.q: A metallic rod breaks when strain produced is 0.2%. The Young's modulus of the material of the rod is 7 $\times$ 10$^9$ N/m$^2$. The area of cross section to support a load of 10$^4$ N is
questions.explanation: Breaking stress $=Y\times\text{strain}=7\times10^9\times0.002=1.4\times10^7$ N/m$^2$; Area $=\dfrac{\text{Load}}{\text{stress}}=\dfrac{10^4}{1.4\times10^7}\approx7.1\times10^{-4}$ m$^2$.

questions.q: A charged particle of mass 'm' and charge 'q' is released from rest in a uniform electric field $\vec{E}$. Neglecting the effect of gravity, the kinetic energy of the charged particle after 't' second is
questions.explanation: $a=qE/m$, $v=at=qEt/m$; KE $=\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2=\dfrac{q^2E^2t^2}{2m}$.

questions.q: The electric field and the potential of an electric dipole vary with distance r as
questions.explanation: For an electric dipole, the field falls off as $1/r^3$ and the potential falls off as $1/r^2$.

questions.q: The displacement of a particle executing SHM is given by $X=3\sin\left[2\pi t+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]$ where 'x' is in metres and 't' is in seconds. The amplitude and maximum speed of the particle is
questions.explanation: Amplitude $A=3$ m, $\omega=2\pi$ rad/s; maximum speed $=A\omega=3\times2\pi=6\pi$ m/s.

questions.q: Electrical as well as gravitational effects can be thought to be caused by fields. Which of the following is true for an electrical or gravitational field?
options: Fields are useful for understanding forces acting through a distance.
The field concept is often used to describe contact forces.
There is no way to verify the existence of a force field since it is just a concept.
Gravitational or Electric field does not exist in the space around an object.
questions.explanation: The field concept was introduced precisely to explain how forces act between bodies separated by a distance, without requiring contact.

questions.q: Four charges +q, +2q, +q and -2q are placed at the corners of a square ABCD respectively. The force on a unit positive charge kept at the centre 'O' is
questions.explanation: The equal charges +q at A and C (diagonally opposite) produce forces that cancel at the centre. The forces due to +2q at B (repulsion) and -2q at D (attraction) both act along the same direction, i.e. along diagonal BD.

questions.q: An electric dipole with dipole moment 4 $\times$ 10$^{-9}$ C m is aligned at 30$^\circ$ with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude 5 $\times$ 10$^4$ NC$^{-1}$, the magnitude of the torque acting on the dipole is
questions.explanation: $\tau=pE\sin\theta=4\times10^{-9}\times5\times10^4\times\sin30^\circ=2\times10^{-4}\times0.5=10^{-4}$ N m.

questions.q: Ten identical cells each of potential 'E' and internal resistance 'r', are connected in series to form a closed circuit. An ideal voltmeter connected across three cells, will read
questions.note: With no external resistor the loop current is I = 10E/10r = E/r, so the voltmeter across any 3 series cells should read 3E - I(3r) = 3E - 3E = 0, which isn't an option; KEA's key credits 3E (the naive sum of EMFs, ignoring that the same current also flows through those cells' own internal resistance).
questions.explanation: KEA's key credits the simple sum of the three cells' EMFs, 3E, though a full loop analysis (see note) gives 0.

questions.q: In an atom electrons revolve around the nucleus along a path of radius 0.72 Å making 9.4 $\times$ 10$^{18}$ revolutions per second. The equivalent current is $-$ [given e = 1.6 $\times$ 10$^{-19}$ C]
questions.explanation: Equivalent current $I=ef=1.6\times10^{-19}\times9.4\times10^{18}\approx1.5$ A.

questions.q: When a metal conductor connected to left gap of a meter bridge is heated, the balancing point
questions.explanation: Heating a metal increases its resistance; to restore balance ($R_{left}/R_{right}=l/(100-l)$) with a larger left resistance, the balance length l must increase, i.e. the balance point shifts towards the right.

questions.q: Two tiny spheres carrying charges 1.8 $\mu$C and 2.8 $\mu$C are located at 40 cm apart. The potential at the mid-point of the line joining the two charges is
questions.explanation: At the mid-point, $r=0.2$ m from each charge. $V=k\dfrac{q_1+q_2}{r}=9\times10^9\times\dfrac{4.6\times10^{-6}}{0.2}\approx2.1\times10^5$ V.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor is charged by connecting a 2 V battery across it. It is then disconnected from the battery and a glass slab is introduced between plates. Which of the following pairs of quantities decrease?
questions.explanation: With the battery disconnected, charge Q stays constant while inserting the dielectric increases capacitance C; since $V=Q/C$ and $U=Q^2/2C$, both the potential difference and the stored energy decrease.

questions.q: A charged particle is moving in an electric field of 3 $\times$ 10$^{-10}$ V m$^{-1}$ with mobility 2.5 $\times$ 10$^6$ m$^2$/Vs, its drift velocity is
questions.explanation: Drift velocity $v_d=\mu E=2.5\times10^6\times3\times10^{-10}=7.5\times10^{-4}$ m/s.

questions.q: Wire bound resistors are made by
options: winding the wires of an alloy of Ge, Au, Ga
winding the wires of an alloy of Cu, Al, Ag
winding the wires of an alloy of manganin, constantan, nichrome
winding the wires of an alloy of Si, Tu, Fe
questions.explanation: Wire-wound resistors are made from high-resistivity, low temperature-coefficient alloys such as manganin, constantan and nichrome.

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance 50 $\Omega$ is connected to a battery of 3 V along with a resistance of 2950 $\Omega$ in series. A full scale deflection of 30 divisions is obtained in the galvanometer. In order to reduce this deflection to 20 divisions, the resistance in series should be
questions.explanation: Current for 30 divisions: $I_1=3/(50+2950)=1$ mA. For 20 divisions, $I_2=\tfrac{2}{3}\times1\text{ mA}=0.667$ mA $=3/(50+R)$, giving $R=4500-50=4450\ \Omega$.

questions.q: A circular coil of wire of radius 'r' has 'n' turns and carries a current 'I'. The magnetic induction 'B' at a point on the axis of the coil at a distance $\sqrt{3}$ r from its centre is
If voltage across a bulb rated 220 V, 100 W drops by 2.5% of its rated value, the percentage of the rated value by which the power would decrease is
questions.explanation: Since $P\propto V^2$, $\dfrac{dP}{P}=2\dfrac{dV}{V}=2\times2.5\%=5\%$.

questions.q: A wire of a certain material is stretched slowly by 10%. Its new resistance and specific resistance becomes respectively
questions.explanation: Volume stays constant, so $A'=A/1.1$ when $L'=1.1L$; $R=\rho L/A$ gives $R'=1.21R$, while resistivity $\rho$ (a material property) stays the same.

questions.q: A proton moves with a velocity of 5 $\times$ 10$^6$ $\hat{j}$ m s$^{-1}$ through the uniform electric field, $\vec{E}=4\times10^6[2\hat{i}+0.2\hat{j}+0.1\hat{k}]$ Vm$^{-1}$ and the uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}=0.2[\hat{i}+0.2\hat{j}+\hat{k}]$ T. The approximate net force acting on the proton is
questions.note: Computing $\vec v\times\vec B=(1,0,-1)\times10^6$ and adding to $\vec E$ gives $\vec E+\vec v\times\vec B\approx(9,0.8,-0.6)\times10^6$ Vm$^{-1}$, magnitude $\approx9.06\times10^6$, so $F=q|\vec E+\vec v\times\vec B|\approx1.45\times10^{-12}$ N ($\approx14.5\times10^{-13}$ N) - closest to option D, not B; KEA's key credits option B.
questions.explanation: Net force $\vec F=q(\vec E+\vec v\times \vec B)$; KEA's key credits a magnitude of $\approx5\times10^{-13}$ N (see note for the full vector calculation).

questions.q: A solenoid of length 50 cm having 100 turns carries a current of 2.5 A. The magnetic field at one end of the solenoid is
questions.explanation: $n=N/L=100/0.5=200$ turns/m. Field at the centre of a long solenoid $=\mu_0 nI=4\pi\times10^{-7}\times200\times2.5\approx6.28\times10^{-4}$ T; at the end it is half of this, $\approx3.14\times10^{-4}$ T.

questions.q: An alternating current is given by $i=i_1\sin\omega t+i_2\cos\omega t$. The r.m.s. current is given by
questions.explanation: For two out-of-phase sinusoidal components of the same frequency, the rms value combines as $\sqrt{\dfrac{i_1^2+i_2^2}{2}}$.

questions.q: Which of the following statements proves that Earth has a magnetic field?
options: The intensity of cosmic rays stream of charged particles is more at the poles than at the equator.
A large quantity of iron-ore is found in the Earth.
Earth is a planet rotating about the North South axis.
questions.explanation: Charged cosmic ray particles are deflected by the Earth's magnetic field and get funnelled towards the magnetic poles, so their intensity is higher there than at the equator — direct evidence of the Earth's magnetic field.

questions.q: A long solenoid has 500 turns, when a current of 2 A is passed through it, the resulting magnetic flux linked with each turn of the solenoid is 4 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ Wb, then self induction of the solenoid is
questions.explanation: $L=\dfrac{N\phi}{I}=\dfrac{500\times4\times10^{-3}}{2}=1.0$ H.

questions.q: A fully charged capacitor 'C' with initial charge 'q$_0$' is connected to a coil of self inductance 'L' at t = 0. The time at which the energy is stored equally between the electric and the magnetic field is
questions.explanation: The charge oscillates as $q=q_0\cos\omega t$ with $\omega=1/\sqrt{LC}$. The energies are equal when $q=q_0/\sqrt2$, i.e. when $\omega t=\pi/4$, giving $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\sqrt{LC}$.

questions.q: A magnetic field of flux density 1.0 Wb m$^{-2}$ acts normal to a 80 turn coil of 0.01 m$^2$ area. If this coil is removed from the field in 0.2 second, the emf induced in it is
questions.explanation: emf $=\dfrac{N B A}{t}=\dfrac{80\times1.0\times0.01}{0.2}=4$ V.

questions.q: A ray of light passes through an equilateral glass prism in such a manner that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of emergence and each of these angles is equal to $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of the angle of the prism. The angle of deviation is
questions.explanation: Angle of prism A = 60$^\circ$; $i=e=\dfrac{3}{4}\times60^\circ=45^\circ$. Deviation $D=i+e-A=45+45-60=30^\circ$.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 'f' is placed somewhere in between an object and a screen. The distance between the object and the screen is 'x'. If the numerical value of the magnification produced by the lens is 'm', then the focal length of the lens is
questions.explanation: With $u+v=x$ and $v=mu$: $u=\dfrac{x}{1+m}$, $v=\dfrac{mx}{1+m}$. Then $f=\dfrac{uv}{u+v}=\dfrac{mx}{(1+m)^2}$.

questions.q: A series resonant ac circuit contains a capacitance 10$^{-6}$ F and an inductor of 10$^{-4}$ H. The frequency of electrical oscillations will be
questions.explanation: $f=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{10^{-4}\times10^{-6}}}=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\times10^{-5}}=\dfrac{10^5}{2\pi}$ Hz.

questions.q: In a series LCR circuit R = 300 $\Omega$, L = 0.9 H, C = 2.0 $\mu$F and $\omega$ = 1000 rad/sec., then impedance of the circuit is
questions.explanation: $X_L=\omega L=1000\times0.9=900\ \Omega$; $X_C=\dfrac{1}{\omega C}=\dfrac{1}{1000\times2\times10^{-6}}=500\ \Omega$. $Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}=\sqrt{300^2+400^2}=500\ \Omega$.

questions.q: Which of the following radiations of electromagnetic waves has the highest wavelength?
questions.explanation: In the electromagnetic spectrum, wavelength decreases in the order microwaves > IR > UV > X-rays, so microwaves have the highest wavelength among the given options.

questions.q: The power of a equi-concave lens is $-$4.5 D and is made of a material of R.I. 1.6, the radii of curvature of the lens is
questions.explanation: For an equiconcave lens $R_1=-R$, $R_2=+R$. $\dfrac{1}{f}=(\mu-1)\left(\dfrac{-1}{R}-\dfrac{1}{R}\right)=\dfrac{-2(\mu-1)}{R}$. With $P=1/f=-4.5$ D: $R=\dfrac{-2(0.6)}{-4.5}\times100\ \text{cm}\approx-26.6$ cm.
